newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carrefour increased stake in GMB - paper.
newsitem.headline: Carrefour increased stake in GMB - paper.

text.p: Carrefour has acquired another eight percent in holding group GMB, which controls the Cora hypermarkets chain, adding to the 33.34 percent it bought last week, business daily Les Echos said on Thursday.
Carrefour declined comment. "We are not making any immediate comment," a Carrefour spokesman said.

In an interview with Les Echos, Cora head Philippe Bouriez, brother of Michel Bouriez and Anne-Marie Gerard who sold their stakes to Carrefour, said he remained composed in the face of this new attack and could count on the support of his other brother and sister.
"I am supported by a majority of shareholders who are organised and unbreakable", he said to the newspaper, refusing to go into any further detail.
"Everybody knows that with its blocking minority Carrefour has no power other than to oppose potential decisions taken at extraordinary shareholders' meetings of the GMB parent company," he added.
He is not hiding the fact that Carrefour's unwelcome entry into GMB led him to reactivate contacts with other competitors who share the same family-held comapany values, the paper adds.
